summary: A creative, digital or brand agency that sells projects and retainers: a statement hero, proof from clients, case studies with measured results, services, how the work runs, the people, and a clear way to start a project. Works for a quiet consultancy-style studio as well as a loud brand studio.

pages.purpose: Say in one line what the studio makes and for whom, prove it with clients and one strong case, and send serious prospects to the project brief.

sections.purpose: A statement headline about the kind of work and client, with the services listed as links so the visitor can jump straight to what they need.
alternatives: media-text: a studio whose work is best shown by one big image or reel
video-player: a motion or film studio with a showreel
fields: One-sentence positioning (what you make, for whom)
One emphasised word in the headline
sections.notes: Statement variant: oversized type, no stock photo. A loud brand studio can instead build a full-bleed colour stage: a chooser of selected clients that repaints the hero in each client's brand colour with its mark, palette and one result (build from hero + button-group; every client colour must be run through the contrast-safe accent helper so text stays at least 4.5:1). Arrow keys move between clients; announce the current client in a polite live region.

sections.purpose: Show at a glance who already trusts the studio.
fields: Caption with a count and a since-year
sections.notes: Grid variant with five columns and tight rhythm. Only logos the client has agreed to show.

sections.purpose: One featured case study told as problem, what was built and the measured outcome, linking to the full case.
alternatives: gallery-section: several projects of equal weight
fields: Short story: the starting point and what was done
Two or three measured results with a period
Hero image of the delivered work
sections.notes: Overlap variant, 3:2 image. Results must be numbers the client has approved.

sections.purpose: What the studio sells, kept to a handful of offers with what each includes.
alternatives: menu-list: services with a starting price and duration
fields: One or two sentences on what is included
Optional starting price or typical duration
sections.notes: Sticky-media variant (an image stays in view while services scroll) on a surface-2 band. A loud studio may set the services in oversized type instead, one per line.

sections.purpose: A browsable list of selected projects; each row opens its case page.
sections.notes: Brand-studio pattern: client names set huge, one per row; hover or focus floods the row with that client's colour from the bottom. Disable the flood under reduced motion; the row must be a single real link.

sections.purpose: A short annual report: a few hard numbers that make the studio's claims checkable.
fields: Three or four figures with unit
Source and date for each figure
sections.notes: Ledger variant with a source under each number. A loud studio can paint each figure in a different colour block of its own palette.

sections.purpose: How a project runs from first meeting to launch, so the buyer knows the time and effort expected of them.
fields: Three to six stages with a title and one sentence
Total duration or number of meetings
sections.notes: Vertical variant on a surface-2 band.

sections.purpose: The people the client will actually talk to.
sections.notes: List variant. Use each person's name as the photo alt text.

sections.purpose: Clients describing working with the studio in their own words.
sections.notes: Carousel variant; three quotes is enough.

sections.purpose: Recent notes or articles that show how the studio thinks.
A large, calm invitation to start a project, with availability and the reply time.
fields: Contact email or link to the brief
sections.notes: Minimal variant: one big link, fine print with the reply time.

pages.purpose: All selected projects, filterable by discipline or sector.

sections.purpose: Title and one line on what kind of work is shown.
Every project as a card or row linking to its case page.
alternatives: list-layout: a typographic index without images
filter-bar: more than about eight projects across several disciplines

pages.purpose: One project from problem to result, so a prospect can see the thinking and the outcome.

sections.purpose: Client, sector, year, disciplines and the one-line outcome.
alternatives: hero: a full-bleed header painted in the client's brand colour
fields: Breadcrumb back to the work index
sections.notes: A brand studio paints the whole header in the client's colour via the contrast-safe accent helper.

sections.purpose: The problem, the approach and what was delivered.
alternatives: media-text: alternate text and images through the story

sections.purpose: The delivered work: identity applications, screens, packaging or photography.
fields: Images of the work with alt text
Brand palette (names and colour codes) when it is an identity project

sections.purpose: What changed for the client, in numbers.
fields: Two to four results with value, label and period

sections.purpose: The client's verdict on this project.
Keep the visitor browsing: previous and next project.
sections.notes: Band variant; can be painted in the next client's colour.

pages.purpose: Each offer in more depth: what is included, typical timing and where to start.

sections.purpose: What the studio does and does not do.
Every service with its scope and typical duration, optionally a starting price.
Answer the usual buying questions: ownership, revisions, payment terms, hosting.

pages.purpose: Who the studio is, how it works and the full team.

sections.purpose: The studio's story and stance in a paragraph, with a photo of the real space or people.
fields: Photo of the studio or team

sections.purpose: Everyone with role and specialty.
Point candidates to open roles.
Every post with date and excerpt.

pages.purpose: A project brief that qualifies the enquiry: what to make, budget band, timing and contact details.

sections.purpose: What happens after the brief is sent and how fast the studio replies.
Pick services, budget and start date; a side panel adds up an indicative duration and starting figure live.
alternatives: multi-step-form: longer briefs split into steps
form-01: a fully custom brief layout
fields: Selectable services with typical weeks and starting figure
sections.notes: Services as a multi-select button group, budget and timing as card radio groups, then name/email/company/message. The live total sits beside the form in a polite live region; overlapping services should not simply add up weeks (longest runs in full, others add part). Validate on submit, focus the first error, end with a reference number. Label the figure as indicative, not a quote.

sections.purpose: Direct contact for people who prefer email or phone, and the office address.
alternatives: description-list: no visitable office, just email, phone and hours

content: Positioning sentence: what the studio makes and for which clients
List of services with scope, typical duration and (optionally) a starting price
Client logos with permission to show them
Two to six case studies: client, sector, year, disciplines, problem, approach, deliverables, approved measured results, images
Three or four studio figures, each with a source and date
The working process as stages, with total duration
Team members: name, role, specialty, portrait
Client quotes with names, roles and permission
Availability for new projects and the reply-time promise
Contact email, phone and office address
Budget bands and start-time options for the brief form
Brand colours of featured clients (only for the colour-led brand-studio look)

styles.name: quiet studio
styles.why: A consultancy-style agency: oversized statement type with one emphasised word, plenty of white, alternating surface bands, a reading-progress bar and count-up figures. Lets the case studies carry the colour.

styles.name: loud brand studio
styles.why: A brand or design studio: grotesk pushed to poster weight with tight tracking, wide container, whole sections painted in the studio's and its clients' colours (each colour contrast-checked).

styles.name: dark digital
styles.why: A digital product or performance-marketing agency whose work lives on screens; dark surfaces make screenshots and dashboards pop.

pitfalls: Publishing client logos, results or quotes without the client's written permission.
Results without a period or source ('3x more bookings' with no timeframe) read as invented; give the period and how it was measured.
Client brand colours used as backgrounds without a contrast check: text on them must stay at least 4.5:1, so route every colour through the accent helper.
A live 'price' in the brief form that reads like a binding quote; label it as an indicative starting figure and say who confirms it.
Colour floods, crossfades and scroll effects that ignore prefers-reduced-motion.
Stock photos of laptops and handshakes instead of the studio's real work and people.
Case studies that are just image galleries with no problem, approach or outcome.
Bilingual sites where one language is a weaker translation; both versions must be written with equal care.
